parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-generated key (e.g. a UUID v4) that makes a retried act request safe (ADR 0030). Required on every POST: the key store is wired in every runtime mode, and a request without the header is a 400 idempotency-key-required. Reuse the SAME key for retries of one logical submit (same body): the first answer, success or business error, is stored for 24 hours and replayed byte for byte with Idempotency-Replayed: true, without running the act again. Use a NEW key for each new submit. Reusing a key with a different method, path or body is a 409 idempotency-key-reused. A key that is not 1-128 printable ASCII characters starting and ending with a visible character is a 400 idempotency-key-invalid. The pattern describes the header as sent on the wire: the key, optionally followed by spaces or tabs, which are HTTP optional whitespace that the HTTP stack drops before the service reads the value (RFC 9110 section 5.5), so they are never part of the key. A 5xx answer is never stored, so its retry runs again; the single-use confirmation token still allows at most one delegation (ADR 0027).
